newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka troops resume offensive against Tigers.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka troops resume offensive against Tigers.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops on Tuesday resumed their campaign to capture a vital highway in northern territory held by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, military officials said.
A Defence Ministry statement said seven soldiers and 50 rebels were killed in the fighting.
The LTTE did not have an immediate comment on the fighting.

Infantry soldiers supported by planes, helicopter gunships, tanks and artillery began moving northwards from earlier held positions north of Vavuniya, which lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.

The advancing troops were confronted by a large group of rebels from prepared defences. Troops retaliated with artillery, planes and battle tanks, inflicting heavy casualties among the rebels, the statement said.
According to ground troops more than 50 rebels were killed and a large number wounded, it said.
Military officials who spoke on condition of anonymity said 53 soldiers wounded in the fighting were evacuated to hospitals in northcentral Anuradhapura, a town south of the fighting.
Troops launched the campaign in May to capture the 88 km (55 mile) highway that links the government-held town of Vavuniya to Kilinochchi.
The government is seeking to capture the highway to ensure a land route to the Jaffna peninsula, where more than half a million Tamils live. At present all supplies are taken to Jaffna by sea or air.
The operation "Jaya Sikuru" (Sure of Victory) had slowed down after three rebel counterattacks in which scores of rebels and soldiers were killed.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east in a war which began in 1983. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed, but LTTE say the toll is higher.
